title: Blue Light on the Wet Floor
genre: indie pop / synth-pop with subtle R&B inflections
theme: Choosing an imperfect real connection over the safe, glowing distance of a curated life.
story: After closing, a night-shift aquarium cleaner discovers that the same stranger has been leaving handwritten notes beside the jellyfish tank. She assumes they are part of an anonymous art project until one note asks her to meet at the staff entrance before sunrise. The stranger is a former friend who vanished after their last argument, now waiting with two paper cups of vending-machine coffee. Instead of reviving the past exactly, they walk home together and agree to begin again without pretending nothing broke.
setting: A nearly empty city aquarium after midnight, with blue tank light rippling across wet tile, humming filtration pumps, salt on the air, and dawn beginning to gray the staff parking lot.
perspective: First person, present-tense narrator: the aquarium cleaner receiving the notes and deciding whether to answer.
motifs: handwritten notes tucked under a squeegee
style_prompt: Indie pop / synth-pop with subtle R&B inflections at 112 BPM; tender, kinetic, hopeful; intimate mezzo-soprano with conversational phrasing; analog synth bass, glassy electric piano, muted guitar, warm drum machine, cello; build from a spare groove into a wide final chorus; glossy nocturnal production with close, human vocal detail.
